channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-24
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 99 news received.

item.title: 1. CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
item.description: Why it matters: CrowdStrike’s $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler would reshape the cybersecurity market by combining endpoint, cloud, zero-trust and threat-intelligence capabilities. CrowdStrike announced the all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, bringing together endpoint protection, zero-trust networking, cloud security and threat intelligence. Jay Chaudhry will remain CEO of Zscaler and join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.

item.title: 2. The EU Chips Act Unlocks €33 Billion in Investment
item.description: Why it matters: The EU Chips Act is unlocking €33 billion across more than 20 semiconductor projects, signaling a major push to reduce Europe’s dependence on foreign chip supply. Europe has unlocked €33 billion to revive its semiconductor industry, with new factories, GaN power-production sites, and packaging and testing lines spread across more than 20 projects. However, commercial production will not begin immediately.

item.title: 3. OpenAI’s chief scientist calls for limiting the pace of AI progress
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s chief scientist is calling for common limits on the pace of AI progress, potentially influencing industry coordination, safety policy and future regulation. Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores for every major model since GPT-3.5 and is asking competing labs to agree on common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.

item.title: 4. Nvidia’s competitors are designing chips with artificial intelligence
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are using AI to design chips that could improve their bargaining power and challenge Nvidia’s dominance in AI hardware. OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are using AI models to design chips that could replace Nvidia GPUs. This development poses a significant risk to the company’s dominance.

item.title: 5. Microsoft’s massive outage exposes testing and capacity weaknesses
item.description: Why it matters: Microsoft’s outage, which took more than 80% of North American gateway servers offline, exposes the operational and capacity risks of widely deployed cloud infrastructure. Microsoft’s final report says a Windows defect went unnoticed for months before overwhelming Microsoft 365 gateway servers. More than 80% of North American gateway servers stopped responding at the height of the outage.
